import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source CSV file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_4.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_5.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/training_9.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
        # Ensure columns are exactly ['start', 'tendercare'] and types are correct
        df = df[['start', 'tendercare']].copy()
        # Convert 'start' to string (date as string)
        df['start'] = df['start'].astype(str)
        # Convert 'tendercare' to integer
        df['tendercare'] = df['tendercare'].astype(int)
        dfs.append(df)

    # Since all source tables have the same schema as the target,
    # we can concatenate (union) all rows
    target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Optional: If duplicates exist and target examples do not show duplicates,
    # we could drop duplicates. But prompt does not specify this, so keep all.

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_60/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
